title: Lesson 20: الْمُثَنَّى — the Dual, Its Two Endings, and أَحَدُهُمَا وَالْآخَر
summary: The dual gets a lesson of its own, and the book's three parallel exercises turn out to be sorted by case: ـَانِ when the word is the doer, and ـَيْنِ when it is the object or follows a preposition. The class works through all three sets, picks up أَحَدُهُمَا وَالْآخَر for one of two and the other, and meets مِنْ الْبَيَانِيَّة, the مِنْ that explains rather than indicates origin — كُوبٌ مِنْ لَبَنٍ is a cup of milk, not a cup from the milk.
key_points: The dual has two endings: ـَانِ where the word carries a ḍamma, as the فَاعِل — مَاتَ رَجُلَانِ — and ـَيْنِ where a fatḥa or kasra is due, as the مَفْعُول or after a حَرْف الجَرّ — قَتَلْتُ حَيَّتَيْنِ، فِي صَيْدَلِيَّتَيْنِ.
This is why the lesson's three exercises look identical in their instructions: each set groups the words by case, first the ـَانِ forms, then the مَفْعُول forms, then those after a preposition.
The ـَيْنِ form covers both the accusative and the genitive, so where there is nothing to call for one over the other, ـَيْنِ is the default.
An answer should normally be given as a full sentence, which forces the pronouns to be worked out — سَأَلَنِي الْمُدَرِّسُ سُؤَالَيْنِ rather than just سُؤَالَيْنِ.
Word order matters for naturalness rather than correctness: putting the مَفْعُول first is grammatically sound but not how Arabic ordinarily phrases things.
كَمْ سُؤَالًا سَأَلَكَ الْمُدَرِّسُ asks how many questions the teacher asked you, not how many you asked him — الْمُدَرِّس is the فَاعِل, and the كَ is the one acted upon.
أَحَدُهُمَا … وَالْآخَر means one of the two … and the other: لِي أَخَوَانِ، أَحَدُهُمَا طَبِيبٌ وَالْآخَرُ مُهَنْدِسٌ. The feminine is إِحْدَاهُمَا … وَالْأُخْرَى.
مِنْ الْبَيَانِيَّة (min al-bayāniyyah) explains what something consists of rather than where it came from: كُوبٌ مِنْ لَبَنٍ is a cup of milk — the cup is milk, not taken out of the milk.

At a higher level each حَرْف الجَرّ carries many meanings — إِلَى perhaps ten, مِنْ around seven — where the beginner learns only one each. The teacher's note: it is an ocean, and one keeps learning until the grave.
فِعْل التَّعَجُّب has more than one accepted construction, and where two forms are both correct neither is necessarily stronger — sometimes they are simply two ways of saying the same thing.
مَاتَ، يَمُوتُ gives both مِتْنَا and مُتْنَا, and both forms occur in the Qur'ān.
عُمَر is غَيْر مُنْصَرِف, so it takes no tanwīn.

Vocabulary: حَادِثَة (accident or incident, as in Urdu), حَيَّة (snake), مُشْط (comb), مِخَدَّة (pillow or cushion), زِرّ with its plural أَزْرَار (buttons), مِرْآة (mirror — not to be confused with اِمْرَأَة, a woman), جُنَيْه (the Egyptian pound), الْبَارِحَة (last night, though commonly used for yesterday), لِصّ with its plural لُصُوص (thieves), كُوب (cup), لَبَن (milk), مَطَار (airport) with طَائِرَة (aeroplane), ذَبَحَ (to slaughter) with دَجَاجَة (chicken), and كَفَى، يَكْفِي (to be enough).
questions: [00:03:08] Q: Why is it the ـَانِ form there? — A: Because it is the فَاعِل of the verb, and the doer takes a ḍamma — which in the dual shows as ـَانِ.

[00:07:00] Q: Why are there three separate exercises when the instructions are the same? — A: Because each group shares a case. The first set is all ـَانِ, and the later ones will be in the other form.

[00:12:00] Q: Doesn't كَمْ سُؤَالًا سَأَلَكَ الْمُدَرِّسُ mean how many questions you asked the teacher? — A: No. الْمُدَرِّس is the فَاعِل and the كَ is the object, so it asks how many questions the teacher asked you.
[00:11:00] Q: Is it wrong to put the object first? — A: Not grammatically wrong, but it is not the normal way an Arabic sentence is phrased.
[00:19:00] Q: Is that word مَرْأَة, a woman? — A: No, it is مِرْآة, a mirror — learned back in the first book.
[00:25:00] Q: Why is it the ـَيْنِ form here rather than the other? — A: Because nothing in the sentence calls for a fatḥa or a kasra specifically, so ـَيْنِ serves as the default.
[00:26:00] Q: Should the answer say my country or our country? — A: The question asked about your country in the plural, so the answer matches it: فِي بَلَدِنَا.
[00:27:00] Q: Can both forms really be used there? — A: Yes — the book gives both as correct. Where scholars differ, each side gives reasoning; but sometimes two forms are simply both acceptable.
[00:34:00] Q: Does مِنْ mean from in كُوبٌ مِنْ لَبَنٍ? — A: No, here it means of. It is مِنْ الْبَيَانِيَّة, which explains what the thing consists of.
[00:30:00] Q: What does لِصّ mean? — A: A thief, with the plural لُصُوص.

quiz.q: Which dual ending is used when the word is the فَاعِل?
quiz.a: مَاتَ رَجُلَانِ — the doer takes a ḍamma, which in the dual appears as ـَانِ.

quiz.q: Which dual ending is used for the مَفْعُول and after a حَرْف الجَرّ?
quiz.a: قَتَلْتُ حَيَّتَيْنِ as an object, and فِي صَيْدَلِيَّتَيْنِ after a preposition.

quiz.q: Why did the book give three exercises with the same instruction?
options: Because each set groups the duals by case
Because each set uses different vocabulary
Because the third is for revision
quiz.a: The teacher had the class spot it: the first set is all ـَانِ, the later ones are objects and then words after prepositions.

quiz.q: In كَمْ سُؤَالًا سَأَلَكَ الْمُدَرِّسُ, who is asking?
quiz.a: الْمُدَرِّس is the فَاعِل with its ḍamma, and the كَ attached to the verb is the one being asked.

options: One of the two … and the other
quiz.a: أَحَدُهُمَا طَبِيبٌ وَالْآخَرُ مُهَنْدِسٌ — one is a doctor and the other an engineer.

quiz.q: What is the feminine of أَحَدُهُمَا … وَالْآخَر?
quiz.a: The form in فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَاهُمَا الْأُخْرَى.

quiz.q: What does مِنْ mean in كُوبٌ مِنْ لَبَنٍ?
options: From — the cup was taken out of the milk
Of — explaining what the cup contains
quiz.a: This is مِنْ الْبَيَانِيَّة, which explains rather than indicating origin.
مِرْآة is a mirror; اِمْرَأَة is a woman, and the two are easily confused in reading.

quiz.q: What is the plural of زِرّ?
quiz.a: أَزْرَار — the buttons of a shirt, in the sentence about buying two.
From كَفَى، يَكْفِي — يَكْفِينِي الْآنَ جُنَيْهٌ وَاحِدٌ, one pound is enough for me now, with جُنَيْه as the فَاعِل.

quran_examples.arabic: وَاضْرِبْ لَهُم مَّثَلًا رَّجُلَيْنِ جَعَلْنَا لِأَحَدِهِمَا جَنَّتَيْنِ مِنْ أَعْنَابٍ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-ḍrib lahum mathalan rajulayni jaʿalnā li-aḥadihimā jannatayni min aʿnāb
quran_examples.translation: And present to them an example of two men: We granted to one of them two gardens of grapevines.
quran_examples.note: A single āyah carrying the whole lesson: رَجُلَيْنِ as a مَفْعُول in the ـَيْنِ form, جَنَّتَيْنِ likewise, لِأَحَدِهِمَا for one of the two, and مِنْ أَعْنَابٍ as مِنْ الْبَيَانِيَّة — gardens consisting of grapevines.

quran_examples.translation: And for he who feared the standing before his Lord are two gardens.
quran_examples.note: The same noun in the other dual form: جَنَّتَانِ here is the subject and so takes ـَانِ, against جَنَّتَيْنِ as an object in Sūrat al-Kahf.

quran_examples.arabic: فَإِن لَّمْ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيْنِ فَرَجُلٌ وَامْرَأَتَانِ ۚ … فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَاهُمَا الْأُخْرَىٰ
quran_examples.transliteration: fa-in lam yakūnā rajulayni fa-rajulun wa-mraʾatān … fa-tudhakkira iḥdāhumā al-ukhrā
quran_examples.translation: And if there are not two men, then a man and two women … so that one of them may remind the other.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's own example for إِحْدَاهُمَا … الْأُخْرَى, on the testimony of women: if one forgets, the other is there to remind her. It also gives رَجُلَيْنِ and امْرَأَتَانِ side by side in the two dual forms.

quran_examples.translation: So he threw it down, and at once it was a snake, moving swiftly.
quran_examples.note: Cited when حَيَّة (snake) came up in the exercise; it also shows فَ twice in the sequential sense taught earlier, and إِذَا.

quran_examples.arabic: وَقَالُوا أَإِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا وَعِظَامًا أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-qālū a-idhā mitnā wa-kunnā turāban wa-ʿiẓāman a-innā la-mabʿūthūn
quran_examples.translation: And they say: When we have died and become dust and bones, are we indeed to be resurrected?
quran_examples.note: One of the two forms of مَاتَ the teacher noted both occur in the Qur'ān — مِتْنَا here; it also carries إِذَا for the future and إِنَّ with its emphatic lām.
